findings.title: join() can leave later flusher processes neither waited-for nor terminated
findings.body: In join(), the loop over self.processes.items() checks the deadline and does `break` if remaining_time <= 0 (lines 338-341) before waiting on/terminating the *current* process. Because this is now a loop over multiple per-shard processes (previously there was only a single process so this bug was latent), if the deadline is exceeded while waiting for an earlier process, the loop exits immediately and any remaining processes in the dict are never joined nor terminated. This leaks child processes (each holding a Kafka producer connection and Redis client) on shutdown/rebalance under timeout pressure, which can accumulate open connections and zombie/orphan processes over time.

findings.title: Division by zero if flusher is configured with 0 processes
findings.body: self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards)) can be 0 if max_processes (derived from the new --flusher-processes CLI option, default 1 but user-settable) is passed as 0. The subsequent loop `process_index = i % self.num_processes` (line 65) will then raise ZeroDivisionError, crashing the consumer with an unclear error instead of a clear validation message. There is no guard anywhere (CLI option in src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py has no min=1 validation, and SpanFlusher.__init__ does not validate max_processes > 0).

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag keys for shard grouping across related timers
findings.body: The 'spans.buffer.flusher.produce' and 'spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes' metrics are tagged with key 'shard' (line 185, 193) holding a comma-joined list of shard ids, while 'spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce' uses the key 'shards' (line 199) for the same comma-joined value. This inconsistency between closely-related timers for the same logical dimension will break dashboards/alerts that expect a single consistent tag name across the flush pipeline, and conflates 'shard' as both a single shard id (used in spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy) and a joined list of shards (used here) under the same tag key, which is confusing and can lead to incorrect aggregation.

findings.title: Dead code: _create_process_for_shard is never called
findings.body: The newly added method `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` (singular) that restarts the process owning a specific shard is never invoked anywhere in the class; `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards` (plural) directly with the full shard list for a process index. This leftover method is dead code and suggests an incomplete implementation of per-shard-granularity restart logic that was intended but not wired up.

findings.title: Added synchronization sleep is a no-op due to global time.sleep monkeypatch
findings.body: At line 15, `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` patches the `time` module's `sleep` attribute globally for the test process. The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` at line 62 (intended, per the comment, 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change') looks up `time.sleep` at call time via the module-level `import time`, so it also resolves to the patched no-op lambda and does not actually wait. This makes the added synchronization ineffective; the test's correctness for picking up the message after `current_drift` changes effectively relies on thread scheduling/GIL timing rather than any deterministic wait, making the test more likely to be flaky rather than fixed.

findings.title: New max_processes parameter not documented in docstring
findings.body: The class docstring for SpanFlusher (lines 29-41) documents `topic` and `produce_to_pipe` parameters but was not updated to describe the newly added `max_processes` parameter, even though the whole point of this PR is to introduce configurable per-shard multiprocessing. This makes the new, most important parameter undocumented for future maintainers.
